tasks.title: Implement the pace calculation

elapsedPercent = round1(elapsedDays / totalDays * 100) clamped to 0..100
expectedCompletedCount keeps full float precision internally and is rounded only at the response boundary (05:71-77)
progressPercent = round1(min(completedCount / targetCount * 100, 100))
paceDeltaBooks = round2(completedCount - expectedCompletedCount); paceDeltaPercent = round1(progressPercent - elapsedPercent)
critical is evaluated FIRST: (daysLeft <= 7 AND remainingCount >= 2) OR (elapsedPercent >= 80 AND progressPercent <= elapsedPercent - 20)
ahead when not critical AND paceDeltaBooks >= 0.5; behind when not critical AND paceDeltaBooks <= -0.5; on_track otherwise

tasks.resolutionNote: Pace classifies against paceDeltaBooks already rounded to 2 decimals, not the raw difference: the granularity is 100x finer than the 0.5 threshold, it stops a float tail like 0.4999999999999996 dropping a goal a class, and it makes the returned number and the returned class agree - the FE can never see +0.5 next to on_track. expectedCompletedCount itself stays full-precision internally (05:71-77); rounding it to an integer flips a 10-book/20-day/7-elapsed/4-read goal from ahead to on_track.

openDecisions.question: daysLeft for expired goals: follow 03_HARD_DEADLINE.md exactly and return null, knowing it silently degrades a shipped FE screen?
openDecisions.specSays: 03_HARD_DEADLINE.md:64-76 — active gets max(0, differenceInCalendarDays(deadline, today)), completed/expired/archived get null.
openDecisions.codeSays: apps/api/src/modules/reading-goals/domain/reading-goal-progress.ts:42 returns an UNCLAMPED difference for both active and expired (isCounting excludes only completed and archived). apps/api/src/modules/reading-goals/domain/reading-goal-progress.test.ts:189-199 asserts -3 for an expired goal. The shipped FE reads that negative value: apps/web/src/features/reading-goals/components/goal-details-view.tsx:62-65 renders 'N days overdue' from Math.abs(goal.daysLeft), and apps/web/src/features/reading-goals/components/list-goal-card.tsx:187-188 does the same. Under the spec both fall through to the plain 'expired' copy. This is a behaviour regression, not a typecheck break — null is already in the type.
options: Follow the spec exactly: null for expired. FE loses the overdue-day count until the FE pass.
Follow the spec and additionally expose daysOverdue in ReadingGoalMetrics so the FE keeps the information without computing it.
Keep the current negative daysLeft for expired, contradicting the spec.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. The spec is explicit and 12_TESTS_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md:170 lists daysLeft in the Definition of Done. Option 2 invents a field the spec never asks for; if the FE genuinely needs the overdue count it should come back as an amendment. Record the FE regression as a known follow-up in the PR body.
openDecisions.answer: FOLLOW THE SPEC. daysLeft = max(0, differenceInCalendarDays(deadline, today)) for active, null for completed/expired/archived. reading-goal-progress.test.ts:189-199 (the -3 assertion) is rewritten in the same slice. The shipped FE 'overdue by N days' copy in list-goal-card.tsx:187-188 and goal-details-view.tsx:62-65 degrades to rendering nothing; the field is already typed nullable so nothing crashes. Recorded as a known FE follow-up, out of scope for this backend pass.

openDecisions.question: Does a soft-deleted (trashed) book stay counted towards its goal?

openDecisions.answer: A trashed book stops counting. Preserve the current SOFT_DELETE_SCOPE.active filter. openDecisions.question: For an archived goal, is result evaluated against today or frozen at archivedAt?
openDecisions.specSays: 01_GET_GOALS.md:121-131 requires result = completed | expired | null for archived goals so history and success-rate survive archiving, but never says which instant decides 'expired'. 02_GOALS_OVERVIEW.md:85-94 puts archived goals into the success denominator through result.
openDecisions.codeSays: apps/api/src/modules/reading-goals/domain/reading-goal-progress.ts:61-70 short-circuits on archivedAt and never evaluates the deadline for an archived goal, so today there is no answer to freeze or not freeze.
options: Freeze: expired iff the target was unmet AND the deadline had already passed at archivedAt. A goal archived early and incomplete stays result = null forever.
Evaluate against today: the same goal flips from null to expired the day its deadline passes, changing a historical success rate without any user action.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. An archived goal is a closed record; a success rate that moves on its own is a bug report waiting to happen. Option 2 also makes 02's bestResult and successRatePercent non-reproducible across days for an unchanged dataset.
openDecisions.answer: Freeze result at archivedAt. The archived goal's result is whatever the lifecycle said at the moment of archiving, persisted, not recomputed against today. Otherwise the success rate on the overview drifts with no user action.

openDecisions.question: daysSinceLastCounted for completed and archived goals: a number or null?

openDecisions.codeSays: No precedent; the field does not exist yet.
options: null for every non-active status, consistent with pace (05:15-19) and daysLeft (03:71-76).
Always a number, computed from lastCountedAt or goalStartDate.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. It puts every non-active goal on one rule — pace, daysLeft, requiredBooksPerDay and daysSinceLastCounted are all null — which is exactly the 'однакова поведінка всюди' the spec asks for, and it stops the FE rendering 'no progress for 400 days' on a goal finished last year.
openDecisions.answer: null for completed and archived, matching pace and daysLeft. Same rule everywhere; no endpoint-local variation.

openDecisions.question: Does GET /api/goals/:goalId return full countedBooks/remainingBooks or capped previews?
openDecisions.specSays: 07_GOAL_DETAILS_BOOKS.md:34-44 allows either: 'Якщо список може бути великим — допускається у detail повертати preview; full data віддавати окремим paginated endpoint', and calls GET /goals/:goalId/books the recommended production variant.
openDecisions.codeSays: The detail already caps counted books at READING_GOAL_LIMITS.countedBooks = 100 (apps/api/src/modules/reading-goals/domain/reading-goal.constants.ts:11-13) and logs a warning when it truncates (reading-goal-detail.assembler.ts:66-71). A goal's snapshot is bounded by its list, which has no size limit.
options: Detail returns a capped preview of each array (reuse the existing 100, or a smaller preview like 20) and /books serves the full paginated data.
Detail returns everything, /books exists only for convenience.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1 with the existing 100 kept as the cap for both arrays, so the response stays bounded and the truncation warning already in place keeps working. /books is mandatory either way (11_SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:74 requires its Swagger, 12:114 requires its tests).
openDecisions.answer: Capped previews. GET /api/goals/:goalId returns countedBooks and remainingBooks capped at 100 each (the repo's existing max page size) plus snapshotBookCount for the true total; GET /api/goals/:goalId/books serves the full paginated set.

openDecisions.question: How do progress_desc / progress_asc / risk_desc sort and paginate, given they order by values no column holds?
openDecisions.specSays: 01_GET_GOALS.md:44-52 requires all 7 sorts; :139-140 requires them to be stable and the cursor to carry enough for deterministic pagination; :137 forbids N+1.
openDecisions.codeSays: progressPercent and riskLevel are derived from the snapshot and the clock — no reading_goals column holds them, so a SQL ORDER BY is impossible without materialising a counter column (which 04 does not ask for). The repo already has a precedent for the in-memory answer: apps/api/src/modules/series/application/series.service.ts:147-158 loads all continuation candidates, sorts them in memory, slices to query.limit and returns nextCursor: null. The keyset precedent for real columns is apps/api/src/modules/notifications/infrastructure/notifications.repository.ts:160-165.
options: Column sorts (created_*, deadline_*) use a real keyset cursor; derived sorts (progress_*, risk_desc) load the user's goals up to a hard cap, compute metrics, sort in memory, and page by an opaque offset cursor. status filtering for active/completed/expired also happens in that pass.

Add materialised counter columns (e.g. reading_goals.qualified_count) maintained by the sync service so every sort and the status filter become SQL. More correct at scale, adds a column the spec never asked for and a new class of drift bug.
Support only the column sorts now and return 400 for progress_*/risk_desc.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1 with an explicit cap constant and a logged warning when a user exceeds it, mirroring the existing truncation warning. Goals per user are bounded by lists, the calculator stays the single source of truth, and it satisfies 'no query per goal' since the whole page is one query plus one snapshot query. Option 3 fails an explicit spec requirement. Option 2 is the right move only if a real user ever crosses the cap.
openDecisions.answer: Keyset cursor for the column sorts (created_asc/desc, deadline_asc/desc). For the derived sorts (progress_asc/desc, risk_desc) load the user's goals up to a hard cap, compute metrics in memory, sort, and encode the position in the cursor. Precedent: series.service.ts:147-158. Rejected the materialised counter column - denormalised state that can drift from the truth.

openDecisions.question: How does the books module reach the reading-goals sync — direct module import or an inverted port?
openDecisions.specSays: 04_GOAL_BOOKS_SNAPSHOT.md:109 — 'Ця логіка повинна бути централізована в reading-goals application/domain service, а не дублюватися у book service.' It does not say how the call is made.
openDecisions.codeSays: There is no event bus in apps/api — grep for EventEmitter/@OnEvent returns nothing. The only inversion pattern is an abstract-class port with a DI token: apps/api/src/modules/mail/domain/mail.port.ts:9, apps/api/src/modules/realtime/domain/realtime.port.ts:8, each with exactly one adapter. Direct cross-module service injection is the common case: ReadingGoalsModule already injects ListsService (reading-goals.module.ts:14, lists/index.ts:1). ReadingGoalsModule imports only Auth/Lists/Media, so a BooksModule -> ReadingGoalsModule import is acyclic today.
options: BooksModule imports ReadingGoalsModule; each write path calls ReadingGoalSyncService.syncBooks(...).
Declare an abstract ReadingGoalSyncPort under books/domain, implemented by reading-goals, so the dependency arrow points from goals to books.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. The ports in this repo exist to swap an infrastructure adapter (SMTP, socket.io, S3, sharp); there is no second implementation of goal sync and no plan for one. Option 2 buys an indirection with no consumer and hides the call graph. Revisit only if reading-goals ever needs to import books.
openDecisions.answer: Direct BooksModule -> ReadingGoalsModule import. The dependency is acyclic today, there is no event bus in the repo, and every existing port has exactly one adapter and exists to swap infrastructure. A port here would buy indirection with no second implementation. CLAUDE.md rule 15: no preemptive scaffolding.

openDecisions.question: Does the bulk reading-status path get wrapped in a transaction so the sync is atomic with it?
openDecisions.specSays: Nothing — 04 assumes a single-book finishedAt change (04:100).
openDecisions.codeSays: apps/api/src/modules/books/application/bulk-books.service.ts:172-186 calls bulkBooksRepository.setReadingStatus with NO transaction, and the repository deletes whole BookReadingProgress rows for N books at apps/api/src/modules/books/infrastructure/bulk-books.repository.ts:327-329. Adding the sync after that call, outside a transaction, means a crash between the two leaves goals counting books that no longer have a finishedAt.
options: Wrap the repository call and syncBooks in one TransactionRunner.run.
Call syncBooks after the repository returns, best-effort, and let the daily job or the next single-book change repair the drift.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. The transaction runner is already injected in that service for updatePagesCount, and a bulk status change of N books is exactly when partial failure is most visible. Option 2 has no repair job for qualification drift — the T39 reconciler only writes expiration activity.
openDecisions.answer: Yes. bulk-books.service.ts:172-186 gets wrapped in TransactionRunner.run so the progress delete and the goal sync commit together. Confirmed by the user: fix all eight call sites.

openDecisions.question: Cadence for the expiration job: daily at a fixed hour, or hourly with an existence guard?
openDecisions.specSays: 10_GOAL_ACTIVITY.md:199 — 'Реалізувати scheduled backend job мінімум 1 раз на добу', and :204 requires idempotency.
openDecisions.codeSays: Every scheduled task in this repo is @Cron(CronExpression.EVERY_HOUR): list-purge.reconciler.ts:24, book-purge.reconciler.ts:24, series/lists/quotes/notes/characters/timeline reconcilers, notification-purge.reconciler.ts:33 and notification-reminder.sweeper.ts:60. There is no daily cron precedent.
options: EVERY_HOUR with the 'no goal_expired activity yet' guard, matching every neighbour.
EVERY_DAY_AT_MIDNIGHT, literally one run a day.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. It satisfies 'at least once a day' with margin, matches the only pattern in the codebase, and closes the window where a user in a far timezone sees the event up to 24 h late. The idempotency guard is required by the spec regardless of cadence, so hourly costs one indexed existence query per overdue goal per hour.
openDecisions.answer: Hourly, with an existence guard on the goal_expired event, following every other reconciler in the repo (list-purge.reconciler.ts:11-26). The spec's floor is once a day; hourly satisfies it and matches the local convention. Idempotency comes from the guard, not from the cadence.

openDecisions.question: Where does the rounding helper live: a new core/rounding.ts or a reading-goals-local one?
openDecisions.specSays: 06_DERIVED_METRICS_AND_RISKS.md:228-237 asks for one rule (percent 1, books delta 2, per-day 3, days/book 1) and no unstable floating-point tails.
openDecisions.codeSays: There is no rounding helper anywhere in apps/api/src/core. Three modules each roll their own: apps/api/src/modules/books/domain/reading-history.mapper.ts:400 roundToOneDecimal, apps/api/src/modules/genres/domain/genre-stats.mapper.ts:35 roundRating, apps/api/src/modules/publishers/domain/publisher-library.mapper.ts:125 roundRating. Three real uses is exactly the threshold CLAUDE.md §8.7 names for extraction.
options: A frozen READING_GOAL_ROUNDING object plus a local roundTo in reading-goals/domain, leaving the three existing copies alone.
Create core/rounding.ts and migrate all three existing call sites in the same PR.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1 for this pass. Option 2 drags three unrelated modules and their tests into a spec-scoped PR, and the three existing helpers round different things (ratings vs pages/day) with different factors, so the shared abstraction is not obviously the same knowledge. Flag core/rounding.ts as a standalone refactor.
openDecisions.answer: Reading-goals-local rounding helper in the module's domain layer. Three module-local copies already exist elsewhere (reading-history.mapper.ts:400, genre-stats.mapper.ts:35, publisher-library.mapper.ts:125); a shared core/rounding.ts is a separate refactor on its own evidence, not a rider on this spec.

openDecisions.question: How many decimals for expectedCompletedCount in the response?
openDecisions.specSays: Contradiction between two files. 05_PACE.md:71-77 says do not round internally and '2 decimals дозволено' in the response. 06_DERIVED_METRICS_AND_RISKS.md:230-236 defines four rounding buckets — percentages 1, books delta 2, per-day 3, days/book 1 — and expectedCompletedCount fits none of them by name.
openDecisions.codeSays: The field does not exist yet.
options: round2, treating it as a books quantity in the same bucket as paceDeltaBooks.
Return the raw float, honouring 05:71 literally.
round1.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. It is a book count, paceDeltaBooks is derived from it and is round2, so any other choice makes completedCount - expectedCompletedCount disagree with the returned paceDeltaBooks by a visible amount. Option 2 violates 06:237 'не віддавати нестабільні floating-point хвости'.
openDecisions.answer: round2, the same bucket as paceDeltaBooks. This resolves the direct contradiction between 05_PACE.md:71-77 (which allows 2 decimals) and 06_DERIVED_METRICS_AND_RISKS.md:230-236 (whose rounding table has no bucket for it). Internal math stays unrounded; only the response value is rounded.

openDecisions.question: booksCounted.currentYear — does the calendar year filter the qualifying date or the goal?
openDecisions.specSays: 02_GOALS_OVERVIEW.md:77-83 — unique books counted towards any goal 'протягом поточного календарного року', not counted twice within one goal, and one bookId across two goals counts once.
openDecisions.codeSays: The field does not exist. The snapshot gives qualifiedFinishedAt per (goal, book), which is the only date available to filter on.
options: COUNT(DISTINCT book_id) over the user's reading_goal_books where qualified_finished_at is inside the current calendar year, regardless of when the goal was created.
Restrict to goals created in the current year.
Restrict to goals whose deadline falls in the current year.
openDecisions.recommendation: Option 1. It is the only reading under which 'не рахувати одну й ту саму книгу двічі' and 'один bookId для статистики' are meaningful, and it is the metric a 'Read for goals this year' card actually wants. Options 2 and 3 would drop a book finished in January for a goal created last December.
openDecisions.answer: COUNT(DISTINCT book_id) over reading_goal_books where qualified_finished_at falls in the current calendar year and the goal belongs to the user. The year filters the qualifying date, not the goal's createdAt or deadline, so a goal spanning a year boundary contributes to both years.

openDecisions.question: Is actualBooksPerDay a number for every status, or null outside active?
openDecisions.answer: A number for every status. The spec (06:92-104) defines it 'for an active goal' and leaves the rest open; the schema allows a number. An achieved rate is a fact about a finished goal, not a projection about a live one, so it does not belong in the same nullable group as pace and daysLeft. averageDaysPerBook is likewise ungated.

openDecisions.question: Does the metrics calculator trust reading_goal_books.qualifiedFinishedAt, or re-qualify at read time?
openDecisions.answer: Re-qualify. qualifiedFinishedAt is a write-time denormalisation and the read is the only place that can notice it lying. A PATCH moving the deadline invalidates every row's qualification; a resync that fails halfway, or a future write path that forgets to call it, yields a wrong completedCount with no error anywhere. Re-qualifying costs one comparison per row on data already in memory and makes the cache an optimisation rather than a correctness dependency. Consequence: metrics.completedCount may legitimately disagree with a stale table, and metrics is the correct side.

sliceLog.reviewVerdict: NEEDS CHANGES -> all three critical defects closed, 8 nits taken

defects.1 DST: reading-goal-projection.ts used bare addDays on a UTC-midnight Date. addDays preserves local wall-clock time, so crossing a spring-forward transition lost a calendar day and the emitted date disagreed with its own projectedDaysDelta. Invisible in CI (TZ=UTC) and live on the dev machine (EEST +0300). Now routed through core/iso-date.ts; differenceInCalendarDays and addDays are gone from that file, so date and delta are computed in the same space by construction.
defects.2 D4 half-done: archivedAt gated the expired branch but not the completed branch, and the qualification window never knew about archivedAt - so an archived incomplete goal could be finished retroactively and flip to completed, drifting the overview success rate with no user action.
defects.3 elapsedDays drift: elapsedDays kept growing after a goal finished, so a completed goal's actualBooksPerDay and averageDaysPerBook changed every day - a 5-book goal finished in 5 days reported 1.0 books/day on day 5 and 0.25 on day 20. Contradicted D14's own justification for the field being non-nullable.

sliceLog.fix: One new domain file reading-goal-window.ts holding two named readings of one concept: resolveReadingGoalCountingEnd({ archivedAt, deadline }) = the last day a finish can still count, and resolveReadingGoalObservationEnd({ archivedAt, completedAt, deadline, now, status }) = the last day that counts as elapsed, built on the first. Defects 2 and 3 are the same statement seen twice - 'for this goal, time stopped here' - and it is now written once. The switch is exhaustive via assertNever. qualifiesForReadingGoal and selectQualifyingReadingGoalBooks now take countingEndsAt rather than deadline, so a caller must say which boundary it means.

review.verdict: NEEDS CHANGES -> all four fixed and pinned by tests
fixed: BulkBooksService.delete trashed books without firing ReadingGoalSyncService, so bulk-trashing every book of a completed goal left it reporting completedCount 5 while trashing the same books one at a time dropped it to 0. The two trash paths gave two answers. It now runs inside TransactionRunner.run and syncs the ids the repository actually soft-deleted.

PATCH /api/goals/:goalId validated targetCount against live list membership (listsService.countActiveBooks), which is exactly the coupling the snapshot removes. Removing books from the list made a legal target unpatchable; adding books let a target through that the snapshot could never reach. It now counts snapshot rows, inside the update transaction, and ReadingGoalInputValidator no longer depends on ListsService.

Archiving narrows the counting window to min(archivedAt, deadline) on every read but never rewrote the stored qualifiedFinishedAt, so a book finished after the archive stayed in countedBooks with qualifies true while completedCount excluded it - one response disagreeing with itself. archive() and archiveSuperseded() now resync the snapshot inside their transaction and recordArchive emits the resulting book_uncounted rows. Migration 20260813180000_clamp_archived_goal_snapshot clears the rows the backfill wrote for already-archived goals; the applied backfill file was left untouched.

The catalog cursor stored {goalId, index} and fell back to the raw index when the anchor was gone. Every item behind the anchor had shifted left by one, so archiving or deleting the last item of a page silently skipped the first item of the next one. The cursor now carries the whole sort key (createdAt, deadline, progressPercent, riskRank, daysLeft, id) and resumes with the comparator, the same shape ReadingGoalBooksService already used. All seven sorts now have an explicit in-memory comparator rather than leaning on the SQL order.
review.alsoTaken: findExpirationCandidates now also excludes goals carrying goal_completed. A goal that met its target before its deadline never earns a goal_expired row, so it stayed a candidate on every hourly tick and permanently consumed part of the 5000-row sweep budget.
recordedNotFixed: remainingBooks ties break on bookId rather than the spec title (07:102-117). Snapshot position is already unique per goal, so the tiebreak is unreachable in practice, and adding a title to the keyset cursor risks the 512-character cursor cap.

goal_completed is written after a non-atomic existsOfType check, so two concurrent finishes can each see the pre-increment count and neither writes the row. Status and result are derived, so the API stays correct; only the activity log loses an entry.
GET /api/goals/:goalId loads the snapshot with its author and cover joins twice, once for the book lists and once to map bookId to title for the activity preview.

overview.completed.completedOnOrBeforeDeadline is structurally equal to completed.total, because a book finished after the deadline can never qualify. Correct by construction, but the FE card will always read 100 percent.

knownSeams.summary: Two date contracts inside one payload in ReadingGoalBookViewSchema.
knownSeams.detail: The picked startedAt/finishedAt inherit bare z.string().nullable() from ReadingProgressViewSchema (books.ts:940-950), while the sibling countedFinishedAt is z.iso.date().nullable() - both ultimately the same book_reading_progress.finished_at column. Runtime agrees today because book.mapper.ts:129 emits toNullableIsoDate. Nothing type-checks a future switch to toNullableIsoDateTime (already used at reading-history.mapper.ts:111), which would ship timestamps where the FE parses YYYY-MM-DD, with no reading-goals test going red. 11_SHARED_CONTRACTS.md:34-46 asks for a single date contract.
knownSeams.why not fixed here: tightening ReadingProgressViewSchema has blast radius over every book view in the repo; it is its own pass, not a rider on this spec.

knownSeams.summary: reading_goal_books.book_id is ON DELETE CASCADE, so the 90-day trash purge silently shrinks a frozen snapshot.
knownSeams.detail: Intended per T8 and the spec's model block, but asymmetric with reading_goal_activities.book_id, which is SET NULL - activity history survives a purge, membership does not. Ninety days after a book is trashed, snapshotBookCount drops by one with no activity row explaining it, landing in the same targetCount > snapshotBookCount state as F1, just delayed.
knownSeams.why not fixed here: it is the spec's own model definition; changing it is a product decision, not a migration fix.

knownSeams.summary: elapsedPercent reaches the risk stage already rounded to 1 decimal.
knownSeams.detail: calculateReadingGoalPace exposes no raw variant and compares the rounded value internally in hasCriticalPace. It feeds only the zero-rate branch of required_pace_high (elapsedPercent >= 50), so the worst case is a goal at a true 49.96 percent elapsed being treated as 50. Every other cross-stage value passes raw.
knownSeams.why not fixed here: widening T15's return type after it was finished and tested, for a sub-0.05 percent effect on one branch.

knownSeams.summary: apps/api/vitest.config.ts does not pin TZ, so date-sensitive suites behave differently locally (EEST +0300) than in CI (UTC).
knownSeams.detail: That asymmetry is what let a live DST bug in reading-goal-projection.ts sit next to three 'UTC day boundary' tests that are no-ops under TZ=UTC. It is repo-wide, not reading-goals-specific: pinning TZ could redden unrelated suites, which is the point, but is a scope expansion this spec should not carry.
knownSeams.why not fixed here: repo-wide test-config change mid-feature; the reading-goals fix makes the code itself TZ-independent and pins the DST cases directly.

releaseNotes: daysLeft becomes null for expired goals (decision D1). The shipped FE loses its 'overdue by N days' line until the frontend pass lands.

Goals can move from completed back to active or expired. v2 adds the hard-deadline upper bound finished_at <= deadline; the current runtime (countedBookWhere) has only the lower bound, so a book finished after the deadline stops counting. Spec-mandated by 03_HARD_DEADLINE.md, and user-visible.
